content: Before starting linezolid, inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and other supplements you are currently using. Specifically, discuss if you are taking any of the following: Cold remedies or decongestants containing pseudoephedrine. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), which are commonly prescribed for anxiety and depression. Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) within the past two weeks, which are used for depression or Parkinson’s disease. Medications for diabetes. Tricyclic antidepressants or bupropion, even if not used for depression. Triptans, such as sumatriptan (Imitrex) or eletriptan (Relpax), which are used for migraines. Buspirone, a medication for anxiety. Opioids, such as morphine or meperidine, which are used for pain management. Overdose Instructions: If you or someone else has taken too much linezolid, seek immediate medical attention. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose Instructions: If you miss a dose of linezolid, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. It is crucial to complete the entire prescribed course of linezolid, even if your symptoms improve or resolve, to reduce the risk of developing antibiotic resistance. Uses of Linezolid: Linezolid is an antibiotic used to treat infections caused by specific bacteria, including: Pneumonia. Skin infections. Certain infections resistant to other antibiotics. However, linezolid may not be suitable for all infections listed above, depending on the bacteria causing the infection. Some bacteria may have developed resistance to linezolid, reducing its effectiveness. Your healthcare provider may also prescribe linezolid for other conditions as deemed appropriate. Mechanism of Action: Linezolid works by inhibiting the growth of certain bacteria. It achieves this by preventing the bacteria from producing essential proteins. Dosage Forms: Linezolid is available as: 600 mg oral tablets. 100 mg/5 mL oral suspension. Injectable forms. Storage Instructions: Oral Tablets: Store at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C). Short-term exposure to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C) is acceptable, such as during transportation. Keep in a cool, dry place in a tightly closed container, protected from light. Oral Liquid: Store at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C). Short-term exposure to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C) is acceptable. Keep in a cool, dry place in a tightly closed container, protected from light. How to Use: Linezolid can be administered as: A liquid injected into a blood vessel. A liquid taken orally. A tablet taken orally. Common Side Effects: The most common side effects of linezolid include: Nausea and vomiting. Diarrhea. Headache. Anemia. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. Other side effects not listed here may occur. Contact your healthcare provider if you suspect you are experiencing a side effect. Serious Side Effects: While less common, serious side effects of linezolid include: 1. Severe Allergic Reactions: Linezolid can cause serious allergic reactions. Stop using linezolid and seek immediate medical attention if you experience: Breathing difficulties or wheezing. Swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat. Trouble swallowing or throat tightness. Itching, skin rash, or hives. 2. Decreased Blood Cells (Myelosuppression): Linezolid may suppress bone marrow function, leading to reduced blood cell production. Attend all scheduled blood tests to monitor this condition. 3. Serotonin Syndrome: Linezolid increases serotonin levels in the body. When combined with certain medications, it can lead to serotonin syndrome, a potentially life-threatening condition. Symptoms include: Confusion or agitation. Headache. Fever or sweating. Abnormal heartbeat. Muscle twitching, stiffness, or spasms. Shivering or shaking. Nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Seek emergency help if you experience these symptoms. 4. Nerve Problems (Peripheral Neuropathy): Linezolid can damage peripheral nerves, causing symptoms such as: Pain, burning, tingling, or numbness in the arms, hands, legs, or feet. Weakness in the limbs. It may also damage the optic nerve, leading to vision changes. Stop taking linezolid and contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms occur. 5. Seizures: Some individuals taking linezolid have reported seizures. Symptoms of seizures include: Muscle twitching, jerking, spasms, or tremors. Stiffening of the arms and legs. Anxiety, nervousness, confusion, or a sense of dread. Dizziness or lightheadedness. Fainting or loss of consciousness. Stop taking linezolid and contact your healthcare provider if you experience these symptoms. 6. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: Linezolid can cause an overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut, leading to antibiotic-associated diarrhea. Symptoms may occur up to two months after stopping the medication and include: Watery diarrhea. Persistent diarrhea. Blood in the stool. Severe stomach cramps. Fever. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if these symptoms develop. 7. Low Sodium Levels (Hyponatremia): Linezolid can cause dangerously low sodium levels, which may be life-threatening. Symptoms include: Nausea or vomiting. Confusion or memory problems. Weakness or fatigue. Breathing difficulties. Muscle cramps. Seizures. Balance issues. Your healthcare provider may monitor your sodium levels during treatment. 8. High Lactic Acid Levels (Lactic Acidosis): Linezolid may lead to a buildup of lactic acid in the blood. Symptoms include: Rapid breathing. Fast or irregular heartbeat. Vomiting. Extreme fatigue. Muscle weakness or cramps. Contact your healthcare provider if you experience these symptoms. Precautions: Allergies: Do not take linezolid if you are allergic to it, its brand name Zyvox, or any of its ingredients. Drug Interactions: Linezolid should not be taken with certain medications. Inform your healthcare provider about all medications and supplements you are using. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: The effects of linezolid on pregnancy and breastfeeding are not fully known. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Food and Drink Interactions: Avoid consuming large amounts of foods or drinks high in tyramine while taking linezolid. These include aged cheeses, sauerkraut, pickled foods, tap beer, soy sauce, red wine, and smoked meats. It is unclear if alcohol consumption affects linezolid. Always consult your healthcare provider for personalized advice and guidance.
